newsitem.title: USA: Hurricane Lili hammering central Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Lili hammering central Cuba.

text.p: Hurricane Lili hammered central Cuba with sustained 90 mph (145 kph) winds and torrential rains on Friday as its effects eased in the island's western region, the National Hurricane Center said.
Forecasters said Lili, which has drifted near the Cuba coast for much of the last day, had dumped 17 1/2 inches (44.5 cm) of rain on the island.
At 1400 EDT/1800 GMT, the center of Lili was located at latitude 22.4, longitude 80.3 west, near the town of Cruces and about 20 miles (32 km) west of the city of Santa Clara.

Forecasters said the storm had moved to the east at about 10 mph (16 kph) during the last few hours but was expected to resume an east-northeast track later Friday, with the eye emerging off Cuba's north coast Friday evening.

The storm's top winds were likely to fluctuate as it moved over land, forecasters said. Sustained winds of 92 mph (147 kph) with gusts to 115 (185 kph) were measured early Friday at Cayo Largo del Sur, near the south coast of central Cuba.
Hurricane-force winds extended outward up to 85 miles (135 km) from the center and tropical storm-force winds extended out about 145 miles (230 km).
A hurricane warning remained in effect for Cuba's mainland from Matanzas province eastward to Camaguey, but was discontinued for the area from Havana westward.
Hurricane warnings remained in effect for the central and northwest Bahamas.
A tropical storm warning for the Florida Keys was discontinued.
The storm threatened to dump up to 12 inches (30 cm) of rain in its path, raising the possibility of life-threatening flash floods and mudslides in mountainous areas, forecasters said.
It also threatened storm surge flooding of three to six feet (1-2 meters), particularly near and to the east of where the center crosses the coast, forecasters said.
